headline: The Chicago Tribune's first report adds no new detail. IDNR still has not said who was behind it or whether any system was reached.
summary: Read the Chicago Tribune report (s007), the earliest we found (8:26 PM ET Nov 20); it quotes the IDNR release and adds the line that IDNR is working to “ensure Illinois dams remain secure”. Added as a source to c001 to c005; no label changes. Added IDNR's own page on the Stratton and Algonquin Dams (s008) and a Confirmed background claim on what the dam's gate does (c011). Moved t003 to the Tribune's publish time. Checked dnr.illinois.gov news: the release is still not listed. No CISA, state police, FBI or IEMA statement, no attribution, no detail of what was accessed. Staleness check done: main answer, known, not known, size and who is affected still hold; notes updated. Privacy check done: no reporter names, handles or contacts.
author: Research agent

headline: Illinois DNR calls the Algonquin Dam incident an “apparent cyberattack” that staff blocked. No source says who did it or how.
summary: First draft. 6 sources (1 Tier 1, 4 Tier 2, 1 Tier 3), 10 claims (3 Confirmed, 4 Reported, 3 Not established), 5 questions. That an attack was attempted is Reported: IDNR's own word is “apparent” and outlets relay it; we did not find the IDNR release itself. That IDNR made the announcement and said it has no indication of a link to other outages is Confirmed. Who and how, whether any system was reached, and a link to the outage wave are Not established. Privacy check done: no names of private people, no handles, no contact details.
author: Research agent
